anomaly_def.Name: Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer persists in choosing or re-using a substantially sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are adequate.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine-level settings for memory, logging, parallelism, and background workers are mis-aligned with the hardware and workload characteristics.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Physical or logical free space for data, logs, or temporary areas is exhausted or about to reach a hard limit.

When these three root causes co-exist, the workload experiences compounding symptoms: 1) plan flips toward full scans or hash builds that spill to disk, 2) those spills contend for a temp area that is already close to full, 3) background checkpoints or log writers configured with aggressive cadence flood the I/O layer, yet fail to reclaim space because log archives cannot be flushed, 4) wait-event patterns oscillate between CPU-light optimizer phases, severe I/O waits on temp or log files, and sudden session aborts with "out of space" or "cannot allocate workfile" errors. Performance becomes erratic; some executions hang in long nested-loop chains, others die immediately once a datafile auto-extend attempt hits the size ceiling. Monitoring dashboards show moderate CPU utilization but rapidly shrinking free space and spikes of internal retries or plan cache invalidations.

Causal chain: a mis-tuned configuration (too small buffer pool, undersized temp and log segments, or over-aggressive parallelism) increases physical I/O pressure and makes the consequences of any sub-optimal plan far more expensive. The optimizer, lacking stability controls, may pick a plan that favors scans and large intermediate results; these results overflow the constrained temp space, accelerating space consumption. As temp or log files near capacity, auto-extend operations or recycling stalls further slow I/O, inflating observed execution costs and provoking the optimizer to switch plans again. Each plan change can introduce new space-hungry operators, which, in turn, push the storage layer past its limits, culminating in space exhaustion, aborted transactions, and pervasive performance collapse.

entry.official_description: Server overcomes the temporary 'out of memory' in '%d' tries while allocating a new chunk of intervals for storing GTIDs.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with insufficient memory headroom, buffer pressure, oversized intermediate state, or memory-allocation constraints inside the engine or client library.
entry.solution_guidance: Check memory availability, per-session memory settings, large sorts or hashes, and whether workload concurrency is amplifying memory consumption.
